finding.claim: Untrusted OAuth `expires_in` (u64) is cast to i64 and added to the current time without saturation, so extreme provider values wrap the stored token expiry into the past and force repeated refreshes (or an overflow panic in debug builds).
finding.evidence: crates/mehh-mcp/src/oauth.rs:50-51 `pub fn mcp_token_expiry_seconds(expires_in: u64) -> i64 { (mehh_ai::now_ms() / 1000) + expires_in as i64 }` and :1224 `let expire_at = new_tokens.expires_in.map(|exp| now + exp as i64);`. `OAuthTokens.expires_in` (:40) is deserialized directly from the token endpoint JSON at :1126 and at crates/mehh-coding-agent/src/mcp_manager.rs:520-529 with no bound check. The sibling implementation in crates/mehh-ai/src/oauth.rs:169-173 deliberately uses saturating_mul/saturating_add 'saturating instead of overflowing on hostile provider values'.
finding.runtimeTrigger: A configured MCP OAuth token endpoint returns {"access_token":"a","expires_in":18446744073709551615}. `exp as i64` becomes -1, so tokens_expire_at = now-1. On the next bearer_token() call, :1252 sees exp <= now+30, enters the refresh path, the server returns the same value, and every subsequent request performs another refresh instead of reusing a live token.

verdict.analysisSummary: Quote check passed: crates/mehh-mcp/src/oauth.rs:50-51 is exactly `pub fn mcp_token_expiry_seconds(expires_in: u64) -> i64 { (mehh_ai::now_ms() / 1000) + expires_in as i64 }` and :1224 is `let expire_at = new_tokens.expires_in.map(|exp| now + exp as i64);`. Independently traced both paths: OAuthTokens.expires_in (:40) is `Option<u64>` filled directly from token-endpoint JSON at :1125-1127 (refresh) and at crates/mehh-coding-agent/src/mcp_manager.rs:520-523 (initial authorization). Neither path bounds the value before the cast; repo-wide search found no clamp. `exp as i64` wraps for exp > i64::MAX (e.g. u64::MAX -> -1), producing tokens_expire_at in the past (:1229 / mcp_manager.rs:536). StoredMcpBearerProvider::bearer_token at oauth.rs:1251-1272 compares that value against now+30 and therefore re-enters do_refresh on every call, yielding repeated token requests instead of reusing a live token; in debug builds the addition can panic on overflow. The sibling module crates/mehh-ai/src/oauth.rs:169-173 uses saturating_mul/saturating_add explicitly for hostile provider values, confirming the intended hardening is absent here. No counter-evidence blocks the chain. Rubric applied: Medium - silent failure in a reachable edge case with a wrong result; not High because it needs a nonstandard extreme provider value rather than a common valid input, and not Critical because there is no unauthenticated exploit or default-path data loss.
verdict.suggestedFix: Bound and saturate the conversion, mirroring crates/mehh-ai/src/oauth.rs:169-173. Replace `expires_in as i64` with `i64::try_from(expires_in).unwrap_or(i64::MAX)` and use `saturating_add` for the current-time offset in both `mcp_token_expiry_seconds` and `do_refresh`, so extreme provider values yield a far-future expiry instead of wrapping into the past or overflowing.
